title: Look at a Clock. The First Second Is Too Long. Here's Why

scenes.text: Look at a ticking clock. The first second lasts too long.
That first tick seems to hang there. It's called the stopped clock illusion.
Every time your eyes jump to something new, your vision cuts out for a split second.
Your brain hides the gap by stretching the first thing you see backward in time.
Scientists in London proved it in 2001. The clock didn't slow. Your brain backdated the view.
Your eyes do that thousands of times a day. Now look at the clock again.

description:
Look at a ticking clock. The first second seems to last too long.
It's called chronostasis, or the stopped clock illusion. When your eyes jump to a new target, your brain fills the brief blind moment by stretching the first image it sees backward in time, so the first tick seems to hang. Researchers described it in Nature in 2001.
Did it work for you? Which clock did you try?
thumbnail_text: THE FIRST SECOND IS TOO LONG
first_comment: Try it with a clock that ticks silently; it works best when you flick your eyes to it from across the room. Did the hand freeze for you?
